note_full: Note. 影響する is kept as 'affects'. It is a causal relation: the Japanese map warns against accepting a causal coupling from correlation alone. The map's test asks whether intervening on the coupling changes the partner's state or process. That test is not written into the definition, so intervention-sensitivity is not presented as a condition every R0 instance must meet. The English reconstruction uses the label 'causal coupling' and retains intervention-sensitivity as a conditional reconstruction-layer proposal. The label and the proposal are not part of the Japanese R0 definition. 状態・過程 is rendered 'a state or process'; the source does not say whether one or both are meant. The link from R0 to R1 is a comparison in the Japanese map; it neither establishes nor denies that R1 requires R0.
note_short: Causal, not mere correlation. Intervention is the map's test, not part of the definition. See note.

note_full: Note. 寄与 is read here as substantive causal involvement in the specified capacity or process: more than correlation, co-occurrence or loose association. It does not require that a single intervention shows a difference, that the whole causal path is traced, that the contributor is indispensable, or that the contributor must be a component of Q. Intervening on the bearer is an important way of assessing a contribution. The depth of a contribution claim is distinguished from the strength of evidence supporting it. Whether 寄与 also suggests a constitutive or foundational role is left as an audit question, not part of the definition. Current contribution is distinct from organizational closure (Fo) and selection history (Fs). The English reconstruction keeps an intervention requirement (decision D-H4) as its own theoretical choice; it is not a condition of the Japanese Fc.
note_short: More than correlation; no uniform single-intervention, full-path, indispensability or component requirement. Intervention is an important assessment route. See note.

note_full: Note. The relation holds relative to a specified Q and to the declared boundary Σ, comparison set 𝒟, mechanism M and time scale τ; a change in any of these is a different claim. The M in the formula is the mechanism, not the M group of the map. 関連性 here is not usefulness or benefit and does not by itself imply meaning or representation. Being comparable within 𝒟 is not the same as an intervention being definable. Intervening on the difference d is different from intervening on Q directly; the map's test asks whether intervening on d changes the consequence for Q. What is intervened on, the path of action and what is evaluated are audited separately. Observation, comparison and intervention are different routes of assessment, and they are not treated as giving equal evidence. Neither a complete intervention nor full identification of the causal path is required for the relation to hold. The English reconstruction's typed Q and intervention_basis are English-side method settings, and its placement of this relation outside the M group does not change where the Japanese map places M1.
note_short: Relative to a specified Q and to Σ, 𝒟, M, τ (M = mechanism). Not benefit. Intervention on d is an assessment route, not part of the Japanese definition. See note.

note_full: Note. 'Passive' does not require that the system has no sensing or action pathways, that such pathways cannot be told apart, or that they have not been identified; whether they exist, can be distinguished and have been identified are separate questions. C0 is not exclusive with C1 (negative feedback) or C2 (specific regulation): they can be attributed in the same system, for example where binding relaxations occur alongside feedback-based adaptation. A stable state should not be read back as a set point or goal, passive relaxation should not be equated with sensing, and whole-system stability is not inferred. What mechanistic restriction 'passive' places on an individual decay route is left open.
note_short: 'Passive' ≠ 'no pathways' or 'pathways unidentified'. Not exclusive with C1/C2. See note.

note_full: Intervention. In the source-faithful publication layer, intervention is treated as an assessment route, not automatically as a constitutive condition of R0, Fc or M1. It can test a relation under a declared intervention design and comparison conditions. A relation is not generally absent merely because no intervention was performed or because its causal path was not fully traced. A null result from a single intervention does not, by itself, establish the general absence of the relation; its evidential significance depends on the intervention design and declared comparison conditions. Being open to intervention is distinct from having been established by a particular intervention. The English reconstruction may retain layer-specific intervention requirements, including D-H4 for Fc.
note_short: In the source-faithful publication layer, intervention is an assessment route, not automatically a constitutive condition; a single null result is scope-dependent.

note_full: Note on the translation. The Japanese original reads 「体系的・組合せ的」. The source leaves open whether every case must be both systematic and combinatorial, or whether the phrase simply lists the two; the English "and" is not meant to settle that question. This rendering is the author's current choice, made after comparing alternatives, and has not yet been reviewed by native English speakers. Other readings and translations are welcome, especially from native speakers and researchers in related fields. Any revision will keep the original text and the decision history.
note_short: Source: 体系的・組合せ的. Both required, or simply listed? Left open in the source; "and" here does not decide it. Author's provisional translation; comments welcome.

note_full: Axis note. This English-side axis carries the systematic aspect (体系的) of the Japanese R4. The Japanese R4 also names a combinatorial aspect (組合せ的; see R4-COMB). The source does not settle whether both are required together; showing them as two axes is not a ruling on that question.
note_short: Systematic axis of R4 (体系的); relation to the combinatorial aspect (組合せ的) is undecided in the source.

note_full: Axis note. This English-side axis carries the combinatorial aspect (組合せ的) of the Japanese R4. As a target-side scope choice it does not carry the R3-like rule (BR3-013). The source does not settle whether the combinatorial and systematic aspects are required together.
note_short: Combinatorial axis of R4 (組合せ的); without the R3-like rule (target-side); relation to 体系的 undecided.
